Overview.
 This program reads a signal from a spectrometer connected to a phone using a microphone input (like AtomSpectra 3, 4 or similar), from an USB-audio spectrometer (like AtomSpectra Nano or similar), or from an USB spectrometer AtomSpectra Pro. If none of them is connected to a phone the program works in a demo mode reading an internal microphone and creating a spectrum.
 
 NOTE: Please add the program to the power exclusion list for proper operation in the background or when the screen is switched off. For the program to function correctly, it is also necessary to grant permission to access the microphone and permission to work with the file system (see below for setting the working directory), and on Android 14 and later, permission to access the location.
 To fully stop the program please use Exit completely menu item.

1. Operating:
 	Spectrum, spectrum change and search modes:
 	- Use navigation Spectrum/Change/Search to switch between spectrum display, spectrum change and search mode.
 	- Use a horizontal pinch to scale channels/energies. Take the fingers off the screen to apply a pinch.
 	- Use a vertical pinch to scale counts. Take the fingers off the screen to apply a pinch.
 	- Use a diagonal pinch to scale channels/energies and counts simultaneously. Take the fingers off the screen to apply a pinch.
 	- Use a left/right swipe to move a spectrum left/right.
 	- Use a down swipe to show and hide an isotope label.
 	- Use a single tap to point a green cursor. Use a slider to smoothly shift the cursor. Tap to the left of spectrum to switch off a cursor. Tap on cursor text to set the cursor channel directly.
 	- Use a double tap to select linear or log10 scale.
 	- Use a long tap to switch between bar and line view modes.
 	- Use kev/ch. button to switch between channel and keV modes in spectrum view.
 	- Use D/I button to switch between kinds of search plot (dose rate or count rate within interval).
 	- Use F/M/S button to switch between search constant (fast, medium, slow).
 	- Use Spectrum/Search button to switch between spectrum and search modes.
 
 	Spectrogram display mode:
 	- Use a horizontal pinch to scale the spectrogram horizontally (channel/energy). Take the fingers off the screen to apply a pinch.
 	- Use a vertical pinch to scale the spectrogram vertically (time). Take the fingers off the screen to apply a pinch.
 	- Use a left/right swipe along the energy/channel axis of the spectrogram to shift the spectrogram left/right.
 	- Use an up/down swipe along the time axis of the spectrogram to shift the spectrogram up/down.
 	- Use a double tap to select linear, quadratic or logarithmic mode for displaying the value (color) scale of the spectrogram.
 	- Use a long tap to switch color palette of the spectrogram.

2. Spectra output:
 	Spectrum mode:
 	- The program can show a main spectrum, a main spectrum with a background spectrum, and a difference between them. All modes are selected using Background submenu.
 	- In the bar view mode the main spectrum is shown blue, the background is shown green, and the difference between them is shown red. The colours are dimmed.
 	- In the line view mode the main spectrum is shown white, the background is shown green, and the difference between them is shown cyan. The colours are bright.
 	- You can clear background data in the program.
 	- You may smooth spectra or revert it by using Smooth in a Spectrum submenu.
 	- You may edit and see descriptions for spectrum and background during cursor output. These descriptions are used as suffix during saving. To change them use Set description in a Spectrum or Background submenu.
 	- The text field cps displays the number of counts during the last second across the entire energy range; the value in brackets is for the energy interval (see the description of searching in the interval).
 	- The text field ~cps displays the average count rate across the entire energy range for the entire acquisition time.
 	- The text field time displays the total time of spectrum acquisition.
 
 	Spectrum Change mode:
 	- This mode displays the change in the spectrum state in a sliding time window. The sliding window size can be selected in the range from 1 to 300 s in the Diff Time parameter in the Settings. In this mode, two spectra with different sliding window durations are displayed: n seconds and 4n seconds (e.g. 30/120). The color of the short window spectrum (n seconds) in this mode is purple, and the long one (4n seconds) is green. The lines displaying the total acquisition time and count rate of the main spectrum are replaced by a display of the window sizes and count rates within these windows (short/long).
 	- The text field cps displays the number of counts during the last second across the entire energy range; the value in brackets is for the energy interval (see the description of searching in the interval).
 	- The text field ~cps displays the average count rate over the entire energy range for each window.
 	- The text field time displays the current size of the sliding windows in seconds.

3. Energy calibration:
 	- The program uses an energy calibration.
 	- NOTE: It is better to switch to channel output before making a calibration.
 	- To calibrate the spectrum point the cursor to the first calibration point, then press a 1 button above the spectrum and enter a value. The button changes from 1 to 2 to show for the second point waiting.
 	- Do the same for the next calibration points. The button will change to - if there is no more acceptable points.
 	- Press √ button to calculate a calibration. Use Store to save the calibration data for the next program start. The program retrieves the calibration data when it deletes a current spectrum. Use Retrieve to apply calibration data to a spectrum from memory. NOTE: if AtomSpectra Pro> is attached, the program will use calibration from the device or store calibration to the device. Internal program calibration does not change and will be restored after unplugging the device or may be changed using appropriate menu commands.
 	- Tap on a nuclide flag on a graph from a nuclide list to set a new calibration point with the nuclide energy.
 	- Tap on a nuclide flag on a graph from found peaks list and enter an energy value to set a new calibration point.
 	- Press on polinom values in Calibration submenu to edit it.
 	- You can set the highest polinom order in the Settings.
 	- Press × button to drop all input points.
 	- Press on a new calibration line in a Calibration submenu to delete it from the list.
 	- You can see a calibration function using Show a function item in Calibration submenu.
 	- Press on Draw new in Calibration submenu to see a new calibration function and calibration points on a graph. New calibration points are shown in green.
 	- You can load a calibration data from another spectrum.
 	- You can select the last channel number to show on energy scale. Channel scale always shows the full spectrum.
 	- You can see and edit calibration data for a current spectrum in a Calibration submenu above the horizontal line.
 	- You can see new calibration data in a Calibration submenu below the horizontal line.

4. Search mode - dose rate/energy range count rate calculation and output:
 The program calculates three values - non-compensated dose rate, compensated dose rate, count rate in a given range (interval) of energies. Non-compensated - linear conversion of the overall count rate into dose rate using a coefficient. Compensated - calculation of dose rate taking into account the energy of the registered photons, the detector sensitivity curve and the coefficient.
 	- The F/M/S button selects the dose rate averaging. F means 'fast', M means 'medium', S means 'slow'. The count values for averaging for each type can be set in the Settings. Averaging is performed using a sliding window based on the number of counts within the averaging window (not based on time).
 	- To switch between value types, press the D/I button. D means 'dose rate history'. I means 'interval count rate history'.
 	- For all value types, the text field cps displays the number of count during the last second across the entire energy range; the value in brackets is for the energy interval (see the description of searching in the interval).
 
 Non-compensated dose rate (mode D, green plot):
 	- In this mode, the count rate across the entire spectrum is converted into dose rate using a coefficient specified in the settings. The conversion is linear, without taking into account the energy of the detected photons or dead time.
 	- You need to set a Sens parameter (cps at 1 uSv/h) in Settings to convert the counts to the non-compensated dose rate.
 	- Additionally you can set a BckgCps parameter to be subtracted from cps in non-compensated dose rate calculation.
 	- The text field dr(n) displays the non-compensated dose rate value.
 
 Compensated dose rate (mode D, purple plot):
 	- In this mode, the dose rate is calculated based on the individual contribution of individual energy ranges of the spectrum.
 	- The coefficients that determine the relative contribution of individual energy ranges to the dose rate calculation are specified in the table available through the Sensitivity... menu item in the Device submenu.
 	- For the calculation, it is also necessary to set the Sens(compensated) parameter (cps at 1 μSv/h). When calculating the dose rate, the count rate in each energy range is multiplied by the coefficient from the table and divided by the Sens(compensated) coefficient. The dose rate value is determined as the sum over all energy ranges.
 	- By default, the coefficients in the table are defined for the AtomSpectra Nano8 spectrometer based on CsI(Tl) but it can be applied for another spectrometers for a rough estimate of the dose rate by means of Sens(compensated) parameter. The curve is fitted to 1 at 661.62keV Cs-137 line.
 	- The text field dr(c) displays the compensated dose rate value.
 
 Interval search (mode I):
 	- This mode is designed to determine the counting rate within a specified energy range (by default, across the entire spectrum).
 	- To set the energy range, use the Energy range parameter in the Settings.
 	- This mode also supports audio alarm of statistically significant changes in the current counting speed relative to the reference level. To enable alarm, check the Enable sound alarm checkbox in the Settings. In the Settings, you can also adjust the alarm volume and select the audio output device.
 	- When the spectrum recording is started with sound alarm enabled, the reference level is calculated first. The reference level calculation is performed until an error of 10% is reached (at a 95% confidence level), but for no more than 30 seconds. After calculating the reference level, the program determines two alarm thresholds: upper and lower. The calculation of the thresholds takes into account the error in determining the reference level, the error in the current count rate value, and the Detection level parameter, which is set in the Settings.
 	- The text field int. displays the count rate in the selected energy interval.
 	- The text field ≈cps displays the reference level value during its calculation.
 	- The text field ♪cps displays the current alarm threshold values.
 	- When the upper threshold is reached, a two-tone signal is played:
 		 1000/1500 Hz at a value not exceeding 2 times the reference level
 		 1000/1700 Hz at a value not exceeding 4 times the reference level
 		 1000/1900 Hz at a value not exceeding 8 times the reference level
 		 ...
 		 1000/3500 Hz at a value greater than 1024 times the reference level
 	- When the lower threshold is reached, a two-tone signal is played:
 		 1000/500 Hz at a level no lower than 1/2 of the reference level
 		 1000/480 Hz at a level no lower than 1/4 of the reference level
 		 1000/460 Hz at a level no lower than 1/8 of the reference level
 		 ...
 		 1000/300 Hz at a level lower than 1/1024 of the reference level
 	- The reference level is displayed on the graph in green.
 	- The upper and lower thresholds are displayed on the graph in red.
 	- To recalculate the reference level, you need to press the ≈ button. Button is enabled only when audio alarm is enabled.

5. Isotope output:
 	- Green cursor line shows the isotope with 3% uncertainty and selects more important isotopes. To see strict line isotopes please use the Show isotopes isotope selection dialog.
 	- The program shows an isotope information in accordance with the channel or keV x-axis selection. In a channel mode the program shows isotope names. In a keV mode the program shows isotope energies.
 	- You can show isotope lines. Note: some isotopes in the list are shown in different colors according to their relative quantum yield on a given line. With increasing quantum yield: dark green, light green, dark yellow, light yellow, red. Light cyan colour is used to show decay chains and isotope groups.
 	- You can select all lines belongs to a given decay chain, all lines belong to a given isotope, or an individual isotope line.
 	- You can select an isotope library. The known isotopes from this library becomes bigger than the others.
 	- A decay chain selection also selects isotopes and individual isotope lines.
 	- An isotope selection also selects individual isotope lines.
 	- An individual isotope line selection doesn't change decay chain or isotope selection.
 	- Isotope lines from the list are shown on a graph with their colors.
 	- Each individual isotope line in a list shows the isotope name, its energy line and a photon output per 100 decays.

6. Isotope detection:
 	- You can find isotopes with the program. The algorithm is sensitive to input parameters, so try to change them to get better results. Created list can be shown on the graph or be hidden. You can change the visibility using Show button (the button will change to Hide). All lines are shown light-purple. The energies of these lines are shown calculated, they are not taken from the internal database. Isotope name is determined using Inaccuracy parameter.
 	- The isotope list is hidden on graph when the spectrum is loaded or you make a new isotope search.
 	- To activate auto isotope search function during a spectrum reading you first need to activate it in Settings. Then open Find isotopes and press Show. An auto update function does not work during a pause or when found isotopes are selected to be hidden. List updates every second.
 	- Input parameters are:
 		● 'Threshold' - a trigger level to add a found isotope to the list (0.00-10,000.00).
 		● 'Window size' - a number of channels to be used for estimation (1-200).
 		● 'Order' - polynomial order (1-5).
 		● 'Inaccuracy' - how coarse will be isotope name definition, in percent of energy (1.00-50.00).
 		● 'Significant bits' - number of bits in channel number to be used. 13 means leave as-is. 12 means combine two channels into one, 11 means combine 4 channels into one, and so on.
 		● 'Library' - library of isotopes to be used. 'All' means 'show even not defined', 'Known' means 'show only defined', others mean corresponding isotope type used by IAEA.

7. Data storage:
 	- You can save main spectrum to view it later. The spectrum is stored in own format file named 'Spectrum-date.txt', where 'date' is the current date. You can add a suffix after date as a note.
 	- A saved spectrum can be loaded in the program via menu. Loading spectrum automatically pauses a spectrum update.
 	- The main spectrum can be exported in a '.xml' format compatible with 'BecquerelMonitor'. The files are named as 'Bq-date.xml' where 'date' is the current date. You can add a suffix after date as a note. If the background is shown on graph it will be also added to the output file as background spectrum.
 	- The main spectrum can be exported in a '.spe' format compatible with other spectroscopic programs. The files are named as 'MCA-date.spe' where 'date' is the current date. You can add a suffix after date as a note.
 	- The main spectrum can be exported in a '.N42' format compatible with other spectroscopic programs. The files are named as 'MCA-date.N42' where 'date' is the current date. You can add a suffix after date as a note.
 	- The main spectrum can be exported in a '.csv' format with a ';' division between fields without energy column compatible with 'Microsoft Excel'. The files are named as 'Export-date.csv' where 'date' is the current date. You can add a suffix after date as a note.
 	- The main spectrum can be exported in a '.csv' format with a ';' division between fields with energy column compatible with 'Microsoft Excel'. The files are named as 'Export-date.csv' where 'date' is the current date. You can add a suffix after date as a note.
 	- Output file names can be modified by Name in Settings. Prefix, date and time can be removed independently.
 	- The background is stored in a single file named 'Background' and is loaded from it or from any other file. Also you may load it to the main spectrum and then move it the background. Note: you can store background only if you have background data otherwise the menu command will be disabled.
 	- You can stop spectrum update by selecting Pause recording in a main menu or on a shortcut bar. After selecting it changes to Continue recording. All impulses received from audio during pause will be lost.
 	- Each saved file can be sent to another program, user or via internet by means of another program with Share a file menu item.
 	- Device settings can be stored using Save device… in Device submenu in a '.txt' format. Device data is stored in an own format file named 'Device-suffix.txt', where 'suffix' can be set or be a date if empty. Stored device settings can be loaded into the program using Load device… in Device submenu.
 	NOTE: Device settings contain a sensitivity curve, most of the parameters in Atom Spectra Settings, and search isotope parameters excluding library type.

8. Storing and viewing spectrograms:
 	A delta is the difference between two subsequent states of the collected spectrum. A spectrogram is a list consisting of a sequence of deltas of the collected spectrum. Thus, a spectrogram allows one to study the dynamics of spectrum change over time.
 	- To save a spectrogram with a specified time interval (delta duration), set the recording interval to a value greater than zero in the Save delta every N sec parameter. A new spectrogram is started each time a spectrum recording begins. The spectrogram file name has the template Spectrogram-"spectrum-description"-"date_time-of-recording-start".txt
 	- You can view the currently recording spectrogram using the View command in the Spectrogram submenu. The first line of the spectrogram appears once the first recording interval elapses.
 	- You can view a previously recorded spectrogram using the command Load from… in the submenu Spectrogram.
 	- To record spectrograms 24/7, there is an option Create a new spectrogram file at midnight, which allows you to limit the size of the recorded files.
 	- When saving spectrograms, full data on all 8192 spectrum channels is recorded. When displayed, the spectrogram data is compressed to 1024 channels.
 	NOTE: Using the spectrogram recording mode results in increased consumption of RAM.

9. Settings:
 	Audio processing:
 	- Graph shows 'as-is' or 'pulse shape' input signal. Select them by swipe left/right. Swipe up/down to scale the graph.
 	- Enable pile-up correction - select to detect impulse pile-up. This parameter tries to compensate the impulse form if the impulse is too close to the previous one.
 	- Use raw audio source - try to use unprocessed audio available on Android 7 and higher. This checkbox is disabled on Android before Android 7 of if the system does not allow to use unprocessed audio.
 	- Invert input - choose if pulse shape is negative.
 	- Source: - choose desired audio input (does not used with direct USB spectrometers like 'AtomSpectra Nano Pro'). Press on text to change audio source.
 	- Min front points and Max front points - minimum and maximum length in counts of the impulse front to detect. Yellow dots on graph show minimum required length on the impulse front, green dots show acceptable length of the impulse front between minimum and maximum number of counts. Default parameters are optimal for all AtomSpectra devices.
 	- ADC is rounded to - number of upper ADC bits to be used.
 
 	Spectrum:
 	- Show as - compress spectrum shown to this number of points. The program reduces 1024 channel of spectrum or the dose rate to the selected number and shows it on graph to speed up the output.
 	- Noise discriminator - do not register channels below this number to exclude noisy channels.
 	- Maximum factor - a maximum polynomial factor for the calibration function
 	- Smoothness - select a realtime smoothness window.
 	- Spectrum - choose sum, peak or average value on spectrum graph during value compression. Peak values help not to loose small peaks, averaging makes a right graph, sum shows spectre as the device has less channels.
 
 	Spectrum change:
 	- Diff time - select the duration of sliding window in spectrum change mode.
 
 	Spectrogram:
 	- Create a new spectrogram file at midnight - with the spectrogram recording enabled, a new spectrogram file will be created every day at midnight.
 	- Save delta every N s - enables spectrogram recording while collecting spectrum data, value defines spectrum delta duration in seconds.
 
 	Dose rate:
 	- Sens - calibration value for dose rate calculation. The value must be adjusted yourself to show the right dose rate value.
 	- Sens(compensated) - calibration value for compensated dose rate calculation. The value must be adjusted yourself to show the right compensated dose rate value.
 	- BckgCps - noise count subtracted from a simple dose rate calculation.
 	- F, M, S - number of counts in sliding window for fast, medium and slow dose rate averaging.
 	- Graph update frequency, s⁻¹ - how often the program updates the dose rate and spectrum data per second.
 
 	Interval search:
 	- Enable sound alarm - enable audio notification of a statistically significant change in the count rate relative to the reference level.
 	- Energy range - limits the energy range when determining the counting rate. Click on the text to select the range.
 	- Output sound device - desired sound output. Press on text to select next output.
 	- Sound volume - sound volume for interval search alarm.
 	- Detection level - determines the level of statistically significant change in the counting rate relative to the reference level.
 
 	AtomSwift integration:
 	- Send data to AtomSwift application - send dose/count rate data to AtomSwift application (which allows you to create maps using your spectrometer). Usage: connect spectrometer, press start button, enable option, run AtomSwift application, select AtomSpectraApp in device list. Minimum supported version of AtomSwift is 1.4.250.
 	- AtomSwift DR - select which dose rate value is sent to AtomSwift application. Non-compensated is recommended for search/maps unless you explicitly need compensated and you know how to configure sensitivity curve.
 
 	Search isotopes:
 	- Auto search isotopes - auto find and show isotopes on a spectrum.
 
 	Files:
 	- Working directory - choose the destination directory for all files. If it shows ... for Android 8 and higher you will be asked for a destination directory. Or you may press on ... (or the name shown) to manually select the desired location. On Android before 8 this parameter can't be changed. If it still shows ... please create directory AtomSpectra in the root of the first storage (usually the phone storage) yourself and restart the program.
 	- Add GPS coordinates to files - add GPS information to output files (spectrum, background and .csv).
 	- Save channels - how many channels from the spectrum to be exported. Note: own format stores all data.
 	- Load channels - how many channels from the old spectrum file to be loaded. If there are more than 8192 channels they will be compressed into 8192 channels or less. Note: new own format has channel number itself.
 	- Channel compression - reduce export channels quantity by combining set value of channels into one channel.
 	- Name - the output files naming. Prefix - file type, date - recording date, time - recording time, suffix - custom text.
 
 	Miscellaneous:
 	- Language - select a program language. To fully apply the program must be restarted.
